product: The world largest dedicated semiconductor foundry, producing 12,682 products using 305 process technologies in 2025 with over 17 million 12-inch equivalent wafers. Portfolio spans 2nm, 3nm, 5nm and 7nm logic plus CoWoS advanced packaging and specialty and mature nodes.
demand: Strong and AI-led. August 2026 revenue was NT$514.81bn, up 53.3 percent year over year; January to August 2026 revenue was NT$3,386.87bn, up 39.3 percent. Management guides 3Q26 revenue to US$44.6-45.8bn, citing the steep 2nm ramp-up and continued leading-edge demand.
pricing_power: Strong. TSMC plans to raise chipmaking prices by 5-10 percent from January 2027 and reported 2Q26 gross margin of 67.7 percent and operating margin of 60.3 percent, reflecting scarce leading-edge capacity and limited credible alternatives.
competition: Samsung Foundry, Intel Foundry, GlobalFoundries and SMIC. TSMC holds more than two thirds of the foundry market as of Q2 2026 and dominates leading-edge nodes and CoWoS advanced packaging, though Samsung and Intel are investing heavily in 2nm and 18A.
team: Chairman and CEO Dr. C.C. Wei; Senior VP and CFO and spokesperson Wendell Huang. About 76,907 employees. Core values are Integrity, Commitment, Innovation and Customer Trust. Credit ratings are S and P AA minus and Moody Aa3, the highest in the semiconductor industry.
market_strategy: Everyone foundry strategy built on technology leadership, manufacturing excellence and customer trust. Expanding global capacity in Arizona, Kumamoto and Germany, adding advanced packaging via the Kaohsiung park ground broken 2026-09-21, and forming the Sony image-sensor joint venture in Kumamoto for 2029 volume production.
bull: Q2 2026 revenue NT$1,270bn, gross margin 67.7%, August revenue up 53.3% y/y, 2027 prices up 5-10%, 2nm ramp and CoWoS lead; dated primary filings and guidance.
bear: Gross margin guided down to 65-67% in 3Q26; 25% US Section 232 tariff from 2026-01-14; PE 28.95 near 52-week high; heavy US$29.44bn quarterly capex risks overcapacity if AI demand slows.
falsifier: 3Q26 earnings on 2026-10-15 showing gross margin below the guided 65% floor or 3Q26 revenue under US$44.6bn.
web_what_changed: Q2 2026 results on 2026-07-16: revenue NT$1,270.38bn, EPS NT$27.25, gross margin 67.7 percent; 3Q26 guidance set at US$44.6-45.8bn. Board on 2026-08-11 approved about US$29.44bn capex and a NT$7.0 Q2 dividend. August 2026 revenue NT$514.81bn, up 53.3 percent year over year. Sony image-sensor JV and ASML 12-inch high-NA photomask initiative announced. 2027 prices to rise 5-10 percent.
web_not_known_yesterday: No new company disclosure dated 2026-09-24 or 2026-09-25 was found. Newest items: Synopsys announced new innovations with TSMC around 2026-09-24 (aggregator); Taiwan broke ground on the TSMC-anchored Kaohsiung advanced packaging park on 2026-09-21. Next scheduled disclosure is 3Q26 earnings on 2026-10-15.
web_demand_price_volume_mix: Mainly demand and volume, led by AI and HPC. Advanced nodes drive mix: in 2Q26, 2nm was 3 percent, 3nm 30 percent, 5nm 33 percent, 7nm 11 percent of wafer revenue; 7nm and below was 77 percent. Price adds upside from a planned 5-10 percent increase starting January 2027.
web_suppliers: ASML for EUV and High NA EUV lithography, Applied Materials, Tokyo Electron and Lam Research for tools, Shin-Etsu and Sumco for wafers. Constraint is High NA EUV availability and readiness: TSMC targets high-volume manufacturing with High NA from 2030 and a 12-inch photomask pilot line by 2031 with ASML.
web_customers: Highly concentrated and shifting to AI. Nvidia is the largest customer at about 22 percent of 2026 revenue, roughly US$33bn, having overtaken Apple at about 18 percent, roughly US$27bn. Others include AMD, Broadcom, Qualcomm, MediaTek and Sony. The top two are roughly 40 percent of revenue.
web_who_loses: Samsung Foundry, Intel Foundry, GlobalFoundries and SMIC lose share and pricing power as leading-edge orders concentrate at TSMC. Fabless customers and AI chip designers lose bargaining power to TSMC price increases. Mature-node foundries face competition from TSMC specialty expansions such as the Sony image-sensor joint venture.
web_contradicting_evidence: Valuation and policy risk. Shares are near the 52-week high of NT$2,535, at NT$2,475 on 2026-09-24, up 84.7 percent over a year, with a PE of 28.95. Gross margin is already 67.7 percent and 3Q26 guidance implies a decline to 65-67 percent. The US imposed a 25 percent Section 232 tariff on advanced computing semiconductors on 2026-01-14.
web_if_management_right: Revenue CAGR approaches 25 percent in US dollars through 2029 with gross margin at 56 percent or higher. 2nm ramps steeply, 3Q26 revenue lands at US$44.6-45.8bn, and consensus FY2026 revenue reaches about NT$5.44 trillion, up 42.9 percent, lifting EPS toward NT$107.82 from NT$66.25 in 2025.
web_if_management_wrong: Margins and utilisation break first. If AI demand slows, heavy capex of about US$29.44bn a quarter creates overcapacity, advanced-node utilisation falls and the 2027 price hikes are resisted. Gross margin already slips to the guided 65-67 percent in 3Q26, and 2nm ramp costs and Taiwan dollar strength pressure profitability.
web_second_order_beneficiaries: Semiconductor equipment and materials makers: ASML, Applied Materials, Tokyo Electron, Lam Research and Shin-Etsu. Advanced packaging and test suppliers such as Advantest. Taiwanese supply-chain names including MediaTek, Delta Electronics and AUO, which is reportedly courted by both Intel and TSMC. AI chip designers and server and power infrastructure suppliers also benefit.
